page: Microsoft Azure EC2es_v6 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the ECEV6 family. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel processor and runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU.

This server does not include local storage, requiring the use of remote storage volumes, though it is designated as Premium Storage capable. There are no integrated GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses included with this configuration. The lack of local storage and hardware accelerators represents a tradeoff, focusing the resource allocation entirely on memory capacity and dedicated compute cores.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high memory-to-vCPU ratio provides a dense memory profile without the added cost of higher vCPU counts. This makes the instance appropriate for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high parallel processing power, such as small-scale databases, caching layers, and lightweight enterprise applications.
